query: How can sellers improve Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: performance_vs_expectation
per_column.rationale: This captures whether the product works as advertised. It is a perceived-quality outcome that sits on the causal path between seller actions (e.g., accurate listings, better products) and satisfaction, not a lever the seller directly sets. It is more a mediator/proxy for satisfaction itself than an intervenable treatment or a confounder.

per_column.name: content_or_creative_quality_issue
per_column.rationale: Describes content/creative quality problems experienced in the product. Again this is a downstream perception on the path to satisfaction rather than an actionable seller-set treatment or a common cause of both a treatment and satisfaction.

judge.rationale: The query is a what-if seller-intervention question: it seeks a lever a seller can SET or CHANGE to raise satisfaction. Neither added column is an intervenable treatment. Both are perceived quality/performance assessments that function as mediators (or near-restatements) of satisfaction rather than actionable levers (e.g., price, description accuracy, packaging, shipping method, support policy). No column plays the role of a confounder (a common cause of both a treatment and the outcome), and none introduces confounders beyond those named in the query. The technical claim for the causal/what-if subtype is therefore not satisfied: there is no settable treatment and no adjusted-for confounders.
